## Natural history notes

A medium-sized wood-nymph moth characterized by its folded resting posture and striking bird-dropping mimicry, with creamy white to pearly patches, brownish shading, and bold dark markings on the wings. In Florida, it is found in forests, hammocks, forest edges, parks, gardens, and other wooded or semi-wooded habitats where grape-family vines and other host plants occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on grape and Virginia creeper leaves, helping move vine foliage into the broader food web for birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
